analysis.question: Compare BASS-II and FLEX
analysis.plainLanguageExplanation: Here is the source-linked evidence for BASS-II and FLEX. Each finding and quantity stays attached to its own record.
analysis.evidenceSummary:
[EV-PSI25-01 · BASS-II] BASS-II SIBAL tests showed limiting flame lengths and low-speed quenching in a small ISS duct. This record uses the documented GMT96-T7 baseline conditions (21% oxygen, 101.3 kPa, 10 cm/s). No numerical spread-rate value is extracted from the plotted curve.

[EV-PSI69-01 · FLEX] In FLEX test FLEX-008 (30CAL06), a free-floating n-heptane droplet in cabin air burned for 14.8 s. The report lists 21% oxygen, 762.4 mmHg (approximately 101.6 kPa), initial diameter 2.95 mm, and a mean squared-diameter burning constant of 0.79 mm²/s. Droplet regression is not solid flame spread.
engineeringImplications: [EV-PSI25-01] Research interpretation (not a measured result): Microgravity eliminates buoyant natural convection (which is ~20–30 cm/s in 1g), exposing a low-velocity regime (5–15 cm/s) where thin fabrics sustain steady concurrent spread, bounded below by radiative/conductive quenching at 1–5 cm/s (with higher quenching speeds required at lower O₂ concentrations).

[EV-PSI69-01] Research interpretation (not a measured result): Spherical droplet combustion in quiescent microgravity is governed by diffusive and radiative heat/mass transfer rather than buoyant convection, with large droplets susceptible to radiative extinction and visible soot shells (in n-heptane) residing inside the outer OH* chemiluminescence flame zone (where visible flame diameters are ~3/4 of LLUV OH* diameters, Section 4.2 p. 15).
limitations: [EV-PSI25-01] Short 10 cm sample length limited the duration of steady spread at higher velocities, and the velocity-stepping procedure could not resolve the flat bottom minimum-oxygen boundary below 16.4% O₂ (NTRS 20150008962 Section 3, p. 7). Exact numeric spread-rate values from Figure 4 are not tabulated as text in the report.

[EV-PSI69-01] Early FLEX tests (including FLEX-001 through FLEX-009) experienced trace fuel-needle conformal coating (Dow Corning 3140 RTV) contamination that minimally affected average burning-rate constants (K) and flame sizes but may have contributed to late-burn droplet disruption (Section 5.2, p. 16). Droplet burning-rate constants (mm²/s) cannot be directly compared to solid linear flame spread rates (mm/s).
Research use only. Experimental atmospheres and flammability boundaries are not recommended cabin settings or operating procedures.

brief:
# FLARE Evidence Brief

Research question: Compare BASS-II and FLEX

## Evidence
[EV-PSI25-01 · BASS-II] BASS-II SIBAL tests showed limiting flame lengths and low-speed quenching in a small ISS duct. This record uses the documented GMT96-T7 baseline conditions (21% oxygen, 101.3 kPa, 10 cm/s). No numerical spread-rate value is extracted from the plotted curve.

[EV-PSI69-01 · FLEX] In FLEX test FLEX-008 (30CAL06), a free-floating n-heptane droplet in cabin air burned for 14.8 s. The report lists 21% oxygen, 762.4 mmHg (approximately 101.6 kPa), initial diameter 2.95 mm, and a mean squared-diameter burning constant of 0.79 mm²/s. Droplet regression is not solid flame spread.

## Reported quantities
- [EV-PSI69-01] Droplet burn duration: 14.8 s (uncertainty not reported). Read the sample-specific conditions in the record.

## Research interpretations
- [EV-PSI25-01] Research interpretation (not a measured result): Microgravity eliminates buoyant natural convection (which is ~20–30 cm/s in 1g), exposing a low-velocity regime (5–15 cm/s) where thin fabrics sustain steady concurrent spread, bounded below by radiative/conductive quenching at 1–5 cm/s (with higher quenching speeds required at lower O₂ concentrations).
- [EV-PSI69-01] Research interpretation (not a measured result): Spherical droplet combustion in quiescent microgravity is governed by diffusive and radiative heat/mass transfer rather than buoyant convection, with large droplets susceptible to radiative extinction and visible soot shells (in n-heptane) residing inside the outer OH* chemiluminescence flame zone (where visible flame diameters are ~3/4 of LLUV OH* diameters, Section 4.2 p. 15).

## Conditions
- [EV-PSI25-01] O₂: 21 %; study range: 16.4–21 % (not a single test) · pressure: 101.3 kPa; study range: 101.3–101.3 kPa (not a single test) · airflow: 10 cm/s; study range: 1–53 cm/s (not a single test) · Microgravity
- [EV-PSI69-01] O₂: 21 % · pressure: 101.6 kPa; study range: 70.9–309 kPa (not a single test) · airflow: 0 cm/s · Microgravity

## Limitations
- [EV-PSI25-01] Short 10 cm sample length limited the duration of steady spread at higher velocities, and the velocity-stepping procedure could not resolve the flat bottom minimum-oxygen boundary below 16.4% O₂ (NTRS 20150008962 Section 3, p. 7). Exact numeric spread-rate values from Figure 4 are not tabulated as text in the report.
- [EV-PSI69-01] Early FLEX tests (including FLEX-001 through FLEX-009) experienced trace fuel-needle conformal coating (Dow Corning 3140 RTV) contamination that minimally affected average burning-rate constants (K) and flame sizes but may have contributed to late-burn droplet disruption (Section 5.2, p. 16). Droplet burning-rate constants (mm²/s) cannot be directly compared to solid linear flame spread rates (mm/s).
- Research use only. Experimental atmospheres and flammability boundaries are not recommended cabin settings or operating procedures.

## Sources
- BASS-II [EV-PSI25-01]: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20150008962 — Report review on file
- FLEX [EV-PSI69-01]: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20150023456 — Report review on file
